figures.finding: The federal Fair Labor Standards Act reaches the Northern Mariana Islands (its "State" includes any territory or possession), and its child-labour provisions do not apply to a child employed as an actor or performer in motion pictures, theatre, radio or television; no territorial permit rule for child performers was found.

value.reachesWritingDirecting: the exemption names actors and performers only; a young writer or director is under the general child-labour rules (29 U.S.C. 212)

figures.applies: US territory; the territory's own labour code was searched for a child-performer rule without result (see blockers).

sources.said: "State" means any State of the United States or the District of Columbia or any Territory or possession of the United States.

The provisions of section 212 of this title relating to child labor shall not apply to any child employed as an actor or performer in motion pictures or theatrical productions, or in radio or television productions.

figures.finding: In the Northern Mariana Islands everyone residing there is of legal age at eighteen; the Code read sets no rule on a minor's performing contract or earnings.

sources.said: All persons, whether male or female, residing in the Commonwealth, who have attained the age of 18 years shall be regarded as of legal age and their period of minority to have ceased.

figures.finding: The Commonwealth Code's own minimum-age section reaches only Commonwealth vessels in foreign trade (no child under sixteen save family-crewed, school or training ships); other work is under the federal Fair Labor Standards Act (see childPerformers).
figures.applies: 4 CMC § 9122 (source 19 TTC § 204), the section the CNMI Law Revision Commission's search returns for "minimum age employment".

sources.said: Children under the age of 16 years may not be employed on Commonwealth vessels engaged in foreign trade, except on vessels on which only members of the same family are employed, school ships, or training ships.
